Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Business and general-news outlets are overwhelmingly focused on Anthropic's blockbuster IPO filing and the broader AI dealmaking frenzy it has unleashed, alongside the Federal Reserve's rate decision, a wave of major earnings, and corporate upheavals including a law firm's possible collapse and GM's stock-exchange switch.

stories.headline: Anthropic files for what could be the largest IPO ever
stories.summary: Anthropic filed its S-1 on Monday, disclosing a $16.3 billion first-half revenue and an $80.7 billion net loss (mostly an accounting charge), with the Claude maker targeting a Thanksgiving-week Nasdaq debut under ticker 'ANT' at a possible $1.5-2 trillion valuation.

stories.headline: AI dealmaking blitz nears $235 billion in a single day
stories.summary: Beyond Anthropic's IPO filing, SpaceX secured $40 billion in debt financing to lease GPUs and Meta said it would seek up to $95 billion in financing for its AI buildout, a dealmaking wave Axios says nearly equals 1% of U.S. GDP in a single day.

stories.headline: Fed expected to hold rates steady as new chair faces inflation pressure
stories.summary: The Federal Reserve under chair Kevin Warsh is expected to leave interest rates unchanged even as inflation moves the wrong way and the labor market stays stable, a mix that bolsters the case some are making for higher rates.

stories.headline: GM to leave NYSE for Nasdaq after more than a century
stories.summary: After more than 100 years on the New York Stock Exchange, General Motors is shifting its listing to the Nasdaq, home to many technology companies, with the move set for November 17 while keeping its 'GM' ticker.

stories.headline: Weil Gotshal taps bankruptcy advisers as crisis deepens
stories.summary: After a marathon partners' meeting over the weekend, the Big Law powerhouse has enlisted Davis Polk to advise on options that reportedly include a last-minute merger, a slimmed-down entity, or a possible wind-down.

stories.headline: China's 'national team' intervenes to stem stock rout, but market keeps falling
stories.summary: The Communist Party deployed state-owned investment funds to try to halt a sell-off in Chinese stocks, but investors are uncertain this round of intervention will work.

stories.headline: Boeing stock sinks as 737 Max production ramp pushed to late 2027
stories.summary: Boeing shares fell 9% after the company said it won't significantly ramp up 737 Max production until late 2027, a disclosure made ahead of its quarterly earnings report.

stories.headline: Honda warns 50% Canada auto tariffs would be 'catastrophic'
stories.summary: Honda cautioned that the industry would face catastrophic consequences if President Trump follows through on his threat to double tariffs on Canadian vehicles and parts from 25% to 50%.

stories.headline: Apple hit by 'Crackgate' backlash over foldable iPhone screen flaws
stories.summary: Apple is facing an outcry over reported screen flaws in its first foldable iPhone, the Duo, a setback the FT frames as a challenge for new chief executive John Ternus; Apple says it will replace affected devices.

Business.gaps: Business Insider and Puck had no relevant recent business items found; Washington Post results returned mostly archived Fed-rate stories rather than fresh 24-48 hour coverage.

US politics.overview: With exactly one week until the midterms, coverage converges on Trump's intensifying campaign blitz, a Justice Department seen escalating politically charged interventions in the final stretch, and nonpartisan handicappers (Cook Political Report, NPR/PBS/Marist poll) showing continued Democratic advantages in both chambers. Secondary threads include Supreme Court immigration rulings, intra-GOP strain over 'fake polling' messaging and fundraising weakness, and a wave of suspicious letters rattling congressional offices.

stories.headline: Trump's DOJ barrels into midterms with lawsuits, raids and arrests
stories.summary: Axios reports the Trump administration is escalating a pre-election barrage of investigations and lawsuits, including a preemptive suit to delay certification of Alaska's Senate race if the Republican loses, and the Omar and Lucas prosecutions critics call politically timed; DOJ denies any 'political paybacks.'

stories.headline: Trump campaigns in Texas and Mississippi as midterm polling shows Democratic edge
stories.summary: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll shows Democrats still holding a slight edge a week before Election Day, even as Trump rallies in Corpus Christi and Lubbock for Senate nominee Ken Paxton and headlines a closing blitz in Mississippi.

stories.headline: Cook Political Report keeps shifting Senate and House races toward Democrats
stories.summary: Cook moved Kansas to 'Toss Up,' New Hampshire to 'Lean Democrat' and North Carolina to 'Likely Democrat,' part of a broader pattern of ratings changes that nonpartisan analysts say reflects growing Republican vulnerability heading into Election Day.

stories.headline: Supreme Court declines to halt DOJ deal ending Biden-era immigration rule
stories.summary: The Supreme Court refused to restore a Biden-era regulation that let judges indefinitely suspend some deportation proceedings, letting stand a lower court ruling the Trump administration had moved to end.

stories.headline: Johnson and Thune echo Trump's attacks on 'fake' polling ahead of midterms
stories.summary: Top congressional Republicans are adopting President Trump's dismissal of unfavorable polls as the GOP tries to project optimism, even as internal party reporting (Punchbowl) describes rank-and-file panic over the environment.

stories.headline: Wave of suspicious letters puts congressional district staffers on edge
stories.summary: A spate of suspicious letters sent to district offices, including one that prompted a police and fire response at Sen. Pete Ricketts' Omaha office, has heightened anxiety among congressional staff just before the election, following separate federal hoax-letter charges.

stories.headline: Massie vows 'week one' vote in lame duck to impeach Hegseth
stories.summary: Rep. Thomas Massie is pledging an early push to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth once the lame-duck session begins, part of a crowded post-election legislative jumble that also includes defense funding and FISA renewal fights.

stories.headline: GOP's hidden online fundraising weakness worsens ahead of Election Day
stories.summary: Politico reports Republican candidates are struggling with online small-dollar fundraising, leaving them increasingly dependent on large donors and super PACs as Democrats continue to out-raise them digitally.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS's web presence returned mostly older archived material rather than items from the past 24-48 hours, so NOTUS coverage here is limited to cross-references found via other outlets' search results.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage is overwhelmingly dominated by Anthropic's blockbuster S-1 filing for its Nasdaq IPO, with nearly every outlet dissecting its financials, governance and risk factors, alongside Google DeepMind's splashy Genie 4 world-model launch. Secondary threads include Apple's rocky iPhone Duo foldable debut, Microsoft's huge workforce buyout, and new OpenAI model releases as the AI arms race between major labs continues to accelerate.

stories.headline: Anthropic officially files S-1 for IPO, revealing soaring revenue and unusual governance
stories.summary: Anthropic filed to list on Nasdaq under ticker ANT, disclosing revenue of $16.3 billion for the first half of 2026 versus $1.2 billion a year earlier, alongside an unusual governance structure that lets its seven co-founders retain 50.1% of voting power even after going public.

stories.headline: Google DeepMind launches Genie 4 world model with audio and real-time steering
stories.summary: Google DeepMind released Genie 4, a world model that adds real-time audio, more realistic simulated environments, and mid-simulation text steering, launching as a research preview for trusted testers.

stories.headline: Broadcom CEO intervened to seal $63 billion Anthropic debt deal
stories.summary: WSJ reports Broadcom's chief executive personally stepped in to close what is described as the largest-ever debt deal to finance AI infrastructure, tied to Anthropic's compute buildout.

stories.headline: Apple's iPhone Duo foldable hit by 'Crackgate' screen complaints
stories.summary: 404 Media reports users of Apple's new $2,000 foldable iPhone Duo are already reporting a visible crease and screen problems just after launch.

stories.headline: Microsoft offers voluntary buyouts to a quarter of its workforce
stories.summary: Ars Technica reports Microsoft is extending buyout offers to employees across the US, Canada, India and the UK, potentially affecting around 60,000 workers, even as the company posted record profit and 30 million paid Copilot seats.

stories.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra, halving API prices
stories.summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6.1 Terra, a mid-range model that cuts API prices in half compared to its predecessor while closing the performance gap with its larger models, which analysts say resets the bar for intelligence-per-dollar.

stories.headline: US government warns hackers are exploiting critical PHP bugs
stories.summary: The U.S. cyber agency CISA confirmed that hackers are actively exploiting critical PHP flaws, software used in roughly 70% of the web, with researchers confirming successful working shells from the exploits.

stories.headline: Meta AI director departs to build an Office and Workspace rival
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports Meta AI director Rohit Patel is leaving after eight years working on AI evaluations and reinforcement learning to launch a startup, Ndoc, aimed at challenging Microsoft Office and Google Workspace.

Tech & AI.gaps: Google DeepMind's own blog (deepmind.google) was not directly searchable this round, though its Genie 4 announcement was reflected via TechCrunch, The Verge, Ars Technica and The Decoder coverage. NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian are search-blocked outlets, so only items present in the provided feed were used for them.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging heavily on the AI/data-center power crunch — from hyperscaler virtual power plant deals to Anthropic's own IPO filing flagging power risk — alongside persistent coverage of soaring consumer energy bills in the US and UK and oil-market jitters tied to Middle East tensions. Utility capital spending, storage/wind deployment forecasts, and rate-case fights over affordability also feature prominently across trade outlets like Utility Dive, Canary Media and Latitude Media.

stories.headline: Oil Prices Fall as Traders Assess Iran Diplomacy, Saudi Attacks
stories.summary: Oil prices eased as markets weighed new diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions with Iran against ongoing Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and risks to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO Filing Flags Data Center Power and Climate Risks
stories.summary: Anthropic's IPO filing devotes extensive space to the risk that it won't secure enough power for its data centers, warning that grid infrastructure buildout is capital-intensive and exposed to permitting delays and financing constraints; the filing also notes climate change could raise operating costs at its facilities.

stories.headline: Google Bets Big on Virtual Power Plants With 1 Gigawatt Voltus Deal
stories.summary: Google and VPP operator Voltus announced a deal to add roughly 1 gigawatt of distributed clean capacity in PJM over the next three to four years, an attempt to prove virtual power plants can scale fast enough to serve AI-driven demand.

stories.headline: Q&A: Why are UK energy bills so high – and how could they be lowered?
stories.summary: Carbon Brief examines why UK household energy bills have continued climbing through 2026 and the policy debate over how to bring them down.

stories.headline: Price hikes aren't all that's at stake in FirstEnergy Ohio's rate case
stories.summary: Environmental and clean-energy groups have filed to intervene in FirstEnergy's Ohio rate case, pushing the utility to direct ratepayer funds toward equitable grid upgrades and demand-response programs amid an affordability crisis and rising outage complaints.

stories.headline: CenterPoint expands 10-year capital plan by $4B to handle load growth
stories.summary: The Houston-based utility is raising its investment plan through 2035 to almost $71 billion and accelerating spending to keep pace with growing customer demand.

stories.headline: BNEF ups US energy storage deployment forecast by 30%
stories.summary: BloombergNEF raised its outlook for US battery storage deployment after hyperscalers' interest in on-site and nearby storage converted into firm orders this year.

stories.headline: Guest post: Greenland ice sheet shrinks for 30th year in a row
stories.summary: Greenland has now recorded its 30th consecutive year of net ice loss, according to a new guest analysis published by Carbon Brief.

Energy.gaps: Argus Media had no feed items and could not be searched due to tool-call limits; The Economist and Reuters had no relevant feed items and block web search, so no current coverage could be confirmed; E&E News blocks reliable recency filtering via search and no fresh (24-48h) items could be verified beyond older archived stories.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Taiwanese and global outlets is dominated by Beijing's efforts to halt a stock-market selloff, the Communist Party's fifth plenum consolidating Xi Jinping's power ahead of a fourth term, and a flurry of China-related diplomacy including a surprise Kim Jong Un visit to Dandong and debate over a possible Trump-Xi-Putin summit. Business and tech outlets are also tracking China's export-driven growth, EV and AI company moves, and a nationalist backlash against Kylian Mbappé over perceived Mao Zedong comments.

stories.headline: Beijing's 'national team' struggles to stem stock rout
stories.summary: Chinese state-owned investment funds have been pouring money into equities to stop a market slide, but investors remain unconvinced the intervention will hold, with Bloomberg reporting indexes slid again on Oct. 27 after a lack of expected 'national team' buying and Nikkei Asia noting state investment is propping up indexes amid weak consumption and AI-related jitters. State-run Global Times pushed back on Western coverage, arguing the AI stock pullback is a valuation correction rather than a 'bubble bursting.'

stories.headline: Xi tightens grip at discipline-focused fifth plenum
stories.summary: Top Communist Party officials gathered in Beijing for a plenum that analysts say will intensify Xi's anti-corruption campaign as he lays groundwork for a fourth term as leader.

stories.headline: Kim Jong Un makes surprise Dandong visit ahead of APEC summit
stories.summary: North Korea's leader crossed into China via the newly opened New Yalu River Bridge for a one-day trip to Dandong, where senior Chinese official Wang Huning called for expanded trade and 'strategic coordination,' a visit timed just weeks before Beijing hosts Trump and Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. State-run Xinhua, via China Daily, said the trip "cemented" bilateral ties around the 76th anniversary of Chinese troops entering the Korean War.

stories.headline: Xi eyes peacemaker role as Trump weighs historic summit
stories.summary: WSJ reports Xi is positioning himself to broker peace talks while Trump has his own agenda for a potential high-profile summit, part of a package also covering Xinjiang's trade pivot and comparisons of Xi's purges to Stalin's.

stories.headline: Mbappé apologizes after Chinese brands drop him over alleged Mao joke
stories.summary: Major Chinese brands cut ties with Kylian Mbappé after a video circulated showing the French football star appearing to joke about Mao Zedong, triggering a nationalist backlash that prompted a public apology, as also reported by Bloomberg.

stories.headline: Taiwan's November local elections seen as test for Lai and Beijing coercion
stories.summary: The Wire China argues that a strong DPP showing next month could boost President Lai Ching-te's re-election prospects and spur greater Chinese coercion efforts, a theme echoed in Taipei Times stories on Lai's rebounding approval ratings and Taiwan's push to counter Chinese election meddling.

stories.headline: China's record export surge expected to cool in 2027
stories.summary: Caixin reports that China's September exports jumped 36.3% year-over-year to a record trade surplus as firms rushed shipments ahead of tax-rebate changes, but economists expect growth to settle into a more moderate pace once that front-loading fades in 2027.

stories.headline: German president's China visit highlights diplomatic pivot beyond Beijing
stories.summary: German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier began his state visit to China in Anhui province, part of a growing trend of visiting foreign leaders looking beyond the capital for engagement with Beijing.

China.gaps: No current distinct coverage found via search for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, CGTN, Yicai Global, or Focus Taiwan; Reuters, AP, FT and The Economist block search so only their provided feed items were considered.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by Israel's knife-edge Knesset election, with record turnout and disputes over voting-hour extensions and Arab-voter turnout claims running alongside a parallel crisis of escalating Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia even as Riyadh, Turkey and Pakistan pursue diplomacy with Tehran. Secondary threads include renewed IAEA pressure on Iran over nuclear access, Egypt's crackdown on independent media, and scrutiny of a UAE diplomat's bid to lead the UN, with scattered business coverage on Dubai property policy and a Saudi investment slowdown.

stories.headline: Israel's election day marked by record turnout and voting-hour dispute
stories.summary: Israelis voted in the 26th Knesset election with turnout running at the highest levels since the 1970s, while the Central Elections Committee rejected a Likud-backed push to extend voting hours and Netanyahu's camp alleged a surge in Arab turnout was being used to steal the vote.

stories.headline: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalate despite Tehran diplomacy
stories.summary: Saudi-led coalition forces intercepted multiple Houthi ballistic missiles and drones aimed at Riyadh and the kingdom's eastern and southern regions, with debris damaging property, while the Houthis claimed strikes on a major oil refinery and an airport.

stories.headline: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials press Iran in Tehran to rein in Houthis
stories.summary: Delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey met Iranian officials in Tehran seeking a regional truce tied to reopening the Strait of Hormuz, but attacks on Saudi Arabia continued within hours of the talks concluding.

stories.headline: IAEA chief urges Iran to restore access to nuclear sites
stories.summary: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told the UN Security Council that Iran must grant immediate access so inspectors can verify the status of its nuclear materials, amid continued stalemate since strikes on its facilities.

stories.headline: Egypt shuts down Mada Masr and convicts its editor
stories.summary: An Egyptian court convicted Mada Masr editor Lina Attalah as authorities ordered the independent outlet's closure, in a country already ranked among the world's leading jailers of journalists.

stories.headline: UAE diplomat's UN secretary-general bid draws rights criticism
stories.summary: Human rights monitors criticized senior UAE diplomat Lana Nusseibeh's candidacy for UN secretary-general, citing her record defending Emirati policy, as scrutiny grows over her path to the post.

stories.headline: Dubai unveils urban policy aimed at boosting property values by Dh20bn
stories.summary: Dubai's ruler announced a new urban development policy intended to lift the emirate's property value by roughly Dh20 billion, part of ongoing efforts to steer the city's real estate growth.

stories.headline: Security concerns threaten to prolong Saudi dealmaking slowdown
stories.summary: Analysts told AGBI that the postponement of Saudi Arabia's flagship Future Investment Initiative conference due to Houthi attacks could deepen an already-weakening trend in foreign deal-making and investment into next year, a slowdown Arabian Business also linked to FII's deferral until 2027.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No distinct, recent (last 24-48h) stories could be found via search for Saudi Gazette, The New Arab, or Iran International; Al Arabiya English results skewed toward older IAEA coverage. Reuters, AP, BBC, NYT and WSJ block search and are represented here only via the feed items supplied (WSJ items used above; no fresh Reuters/AP/BBC/NYT feed items were provided for this beat).

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage across African outlets this week is dominated by escalating conflicts and political uncertainty — Sudan's devastated El Fasher, DRC's Kabila-Tshisekedi showdown, and simmering Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions — alongside economic stories on Nigeria's reform push, Ghana's Ponzi-scheme fallout, and fresh investment deals in Madagascar's mining and energy sector.

stories.headline: Sudan's El Fasher, one year on: Hemeti's bloody prize is now a ghost town ruled by guns
stories.summary: A year after the RSF captured Darfur's last major army stronghold, most residents have fled El Fasher, civilian institutions have collapsed, and armed commanders now hold the real power.

stories.headline: DRC's former leader Kabila is Rwandan 'proxy,' Tshisekedi tells lawmakers
stories.summary: President Tshisekedi told parliament that former president Joseph Kabila is acting as a Rwandan stooge after Kabila joined forces this month with the Kigali-backed M23 rebel group; Africa Confidential had earlier reported that Kabila took command of a front explicitly aimed at ousting Tshisekedi.

stories.headline: Paul Biya: Power at a standstill in Cameroon
stories.summary: Cameroon's 93-year-old President Paul Biya has promised change but made no cabinet reshuffle, creating a vice-presidential post while leaving it unfilled and leaving the country guessing about succession.

stories.headline: Abiy's gains intensify frontier pressure between Ethiopia and Eritrea
stories.summary: Africa Confidential reports that federal Ethiopian military advances have sharpened fears of a wider war with Eritrea, as mediators try to keep domestic conflict from escalating into a cross-border confrontation.

stories.headline: Nigeria's economy 'needs a coach, not just a referee'
stories.summary: Having stabilised Nigeria's macroeconomy, President Tinubu now faces the tougher task of building globally competitive industries without entrenching the advantages of existing industrial giants; African Business separately reports Abuja unveiled a $78bn investor 'deal room' at the IMF/World Bank meetings to court foreign capital.

stories.headline: Get rich or get ruined: Ghana's youth caught in Africa's Ponzi trap
stories.summary: Investment apps that promised to triple Ghanaian savers' money within 40 days have collapsed, leaving young people in financial ruin and exposing regulators' struggle to rein in the online investment schemes fueling the crisis.

stories.headline: Gemcorp joins Madagascar to raise $5bn for energy, mining
stories.summary: Madagascar is teaming up with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management to raise as much as $5 billion to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects on the island, according to a Bloomberg report carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Nigeria jail conditions blamed for deaths of 33 miners
stories.summary: Investigators found that cruel and inhumane jail conditions led to the deaths of 33 young men arrested on suspicion of illegal gold mining in central Nigeria.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no coverage within the last 48 hours (only older PDF issues were available). Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feeds, so their current Africa coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media trade press is dominated by the fight between the global news industry and Meta over new terms of service that would allow broad AI scraping of news content, alongside ongoing coverage of Trump's $10 billion defamation suit against the BBC, a fresh wave of newsroom layoffs, and consolidation moves in ad tech. Entertainment trades (Variety, Deadline, THR, TheWrap) are mostly focused on routine industry news, awards and streaming deals rather than major breaking stories.

stories.headline: Meta delays rollout of new terms allowing broad scraping of news sites amid global publisher backlash
stories.summary: Meta pushed back the effective date of new business-account terms of service to November 20 after mounting pressure from publishers worldwide, though legal experts remain skeptical the delay addresses underlying concerns about AI scraping of news content. Norwegian outlets including Schibsted and NRK are separately seeking a court injunction to block the terms, and US Senator Adam Schiff has urged Meta to scrap them entirely.

stories.headline: Trump ordered to sit for deposition in $10B BBC defamation suit by December 11
stories.summary: CJR examines how the BBC is aggressively using the legal process to fight Trump's Florida defamation lawsuit over the edited Panorama documentary, after a judge recently ordered Trump to sit for a deposition by December 11 or face possible sanctions.

stories.headline: Journalism job cuts tracker: Telegraph to cut around 100 roles
stories.summary: Press Gazette's rolling 2026 layoffs tracker shows the Telegraph planning to cut roughly 100 jobs, part of a wider wave of newsroom redundancies across the industry this year.

stories.headline: Is Skydance's Ellison playing favorites between CNN and CBS?
stories.summary: Mediaite reports that executives at CNN and CBS News both received word about employee buyouts and return-to-office mandates, but the plans are unfolding differently at each network under Skydance's David Ellison, raising questions about unequal treatment of the two newsrooms.

stories.headline: NBC News names Kevin Delaney head of digital content and subscription
stories.summary: NBC News has tapped Quartz co-founder Kevin Delaney for a newly created digital leadership role, filling a position left vacant since its former digital chief departed.

stories.headline: Celebrity seeking injunction against Guardian and ITN cites 'fear of trial by media'
stories.summary: A court heard that an unnamed 'famous' man seeking an injunction against the Guardian and ITN made a suicide attempt after receiving right-of-reply letters ahead of planned reporting.

stories.headline: Midterm political ad spending hits record $11.21 billion
stories.summary: The 2026 midterm election cycle has already surpassed 2024 presidential-year ad spending, with broadcast TV expected to capture the largest share, a surge that Digiday notes is also squeezing regional advertisers' holiday CTV plans.

Media.gaps: Could not find recent (last 48h) news-specific stories from Status or Puck; search results for both returned mostly general/about-page content rather than current reporting. NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so their current coverage could not be assessed.
